THIS CRL.P IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 CR.P.C BY THE ADVOCATE FOR THE PETITIONER PRAYING THAT THIS HON'BLE COURT MAY BE PLEASED TO QUASH THE PROCEEDINGS IN C.C.NO.18548/2018 REGISTERED BY THE VIJAYANAGAR POLICE FOR THE OFFENCE PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTION 406,417,418,419,420 AND 120(B) READ WITH 34 OF IPC NOW PENDING ON THE FILE OF XXIV ADDL.C.M.M.,
BENGALURU.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.
This petition is filed challenging the initiation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners herein.

2. Sri.B.Nanjundaiah - the husband of the first petitioner and the brother-in-law of the second petitioner presented a complaint under Section 200 of the Cr.P.C. contending that certain agricultural properties situated in Madavara village, Dasanapura Hobli, had been bequeathed by Appaiayanna to him and his wife (first petitioner) under a registered Will dated 09.10.1980 and on the basis of the Will, mutation was also made out in favor of his wife.

3. He contended that his wife had colluded with her brother i.e., the second petitioner and had sold 27 NC: 2024:KHC:21103 guntas in Sy.No.79/2 to one Smt.Sujatha on the 13.12.2004 and this amounted to cheating.

He submitted that he and his wife had executed a General Power of Attorney (GPA) in favour of Sri.B.V. Venkatesh in respect of site Nos.1 and 2 and said Sri.B.V. Venkatesh was demanding the execution of a sale deed and he had, therefore, asked his wife to execute a registered sale deed in his favor, but she did not come forward, and on the other hand, she had executed a release deed in favor of her brother.
He, therefore, contended that his wife and his brother-in-law had committed criminal offences by execution of the release deed.
4. Learned counsel for the second respondent also made several other allegations regarding the properties that he contended belonged to him and to his wife.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners places on record a suit filed by the second respondent in O.S.
No.73 2014 whereby, he had sought for a declaration that he is NC: 2024:KHC:21103 the absolute Smt. Rudramma vs The State Of Karnataka By on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150099023/
2 owner of the suit properties by virtue of the registered Will dated the 09.10.1980.
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that as a matter of fact, the registered Will that is executed by Appaiayanna was only in favor of the first petitioner exclusively and there was no bequest made in favor of the complainant - second respondent.
He also placed reliance on the Will that has been annexed to the petition.

7. In my view, since the second respondent contends that there is a Will in his favour and since he has already approached the Civil Court in O.S. No.73/2014, it is obvious that the criminal proceedings that has been initiated against his wife and his brother-in-law would be untenable and would only be an attempt to pressurize them into a settlement.
I am, therefore, of the view that the proceedings against the petitioners are unsustainable and the same are quashed.

Petition is,
accordingly, allowed.
In view of disposal of main petition, pending I.A. does not survive for consideration and is accordingly disposed of.
